admission.justification: A cap was the open question of version 1 and was decided against on the models' own limits; a later change that adds a limit to the transport has to change the models first.

alternatives.option: No cap on the size of a valid answer; waiting, time and reclamation are bounded instead.
alternatives.reason: The existing response models set no finite limit on a worklist or on its list of read files, so a cap would refuse answers that are valid today (rule 5 of version 2 of the requirement).

alternatives.option: Cap the bytes of a child's answer.
alternatives.reason: It would refuse answers that the response models accept, for a large leaf whose worklist is correct.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The response models set a finite limit on a worklist or on its list of read files.

consequences: The parent drains the child's pipes in slices, so an answer larger than a pipe buffer arrives whole.
The request's deadline and the stop of the child's process group bound time and reclamation.
context: A child returns the worklist and the list of the files it read through a pipe. Version 1 of the requirement left open whether the size of an answer should be capped (truth gap G3).
decider: the architect under DEVELOPER-DIRECTION D47 (MIK-R42@v2 rule 5 and the closed gap G3)
